adds.rationale: Nvidia's May 24 2023 Q1 FY24 print confirmed the AI buildup is broadening into hardware demand with a record data-center revenue beat and 'surging demand' commentary, the clearest direct infrastructure play on the dominant AI wave.

news_evidence.summary: Nvidia Q1 FY24 data-center revenue hit a record $4.28B; CEO cites 'surging demand' for AI chips and a trillion-dollar shift to accelerated computing.
Nvidia Q1 FY2024 press release confirms record data-center revenue driven by generative-AI and LLM demand from cloud vendors.

removes.rationale: Google's Bard rollout at I/O remains a reactive catch-up to Microsoft/OpenAI rather than a proactive AI-infrastructure lead, making it the weaker-conviction AI name; swapping it for NVDA rotates toward the more direct hardware-layer beneficiary of the same wave without exiting AI (MSFT stays as the platform-layer holding).

news_evidence.summary: At Google I/O 2023, Google ended Bard's waitlist and added images/app integrations as it 'scrambled to keep up with rival Microsoft', already shipping OpenAI-powered Copilot.

rationale_overall: The watchlist stays AI-dominant but rotates one seat from software-layer catch-up (GOOGL) to hardware-layer confirmation (NVDA) on Nvidia's in-window May 24 data-center earnings surge, the single clearest 'buildup broadening' signal of the quarter. MSFT is kept given its aggressive Build/Copilot push, and LMT is kept as the sole geopolitical/defense diversifier with steady Q1 sales and continued Ukraine-related demand. Result: MSFT, LMT, NVDA.
